qt: to the Commission Tineke Strik (Verts/ALE), Anna Strolenberg (Verts/ALE) Subject:

On 21 September 2026, the Dutch Safety Board concluded that approximately 7 000 children in emergency asylum accommodation are systematically exposed to unsafe living conditions that pose serious risks to their development1. Over 60 % of reception centres are now acting as emergency accommodation; children sometimes stay in such centres for years. 1.

Does the Commission consider the circumstances identified by the Dutch Safety Board to be compatible with the applicable EU obligations regarding the reception of minors, both under Directive 2013/33/EU for the period prior to 12 June 2026 and under Directive (EU) 2024/1346 after that date, in particular with regard to an adequate standard of living, physical and mental health, protection from violence, education, special reception needs and the best interests of the child, and if so, how?

Has the Netherlands informed the Commission, in accordance with Article 20(10) and Article 32 of the Reception Directive (Directive (EU) 2024/1346), about the use of alternative reception facilities due to a temporary saturation of regular capacity, and how does the Commission reconcile the requirement that such derogations be temporary and as short as possible with the structural use of emergency reception in the Netherlands since 2021?

Also taking account of the EUAA’s monitoring of reception conditions2 in the Netherlands, does the Commission consider itself to be sufficiently informed at this stage to assess the conformity of these reception conditions with EU law? If not, what specific information is still lacking and when will that assessment be completed?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.11.2026) Under Directives 2013/331 and 2024/13462, applicable from 12 June 2026, Member States must ensure that all applicants, and notably minors, have access to an adequate standard of living, healthcare including mental health support, education, and are protected from violence. In all decisions affecting minors, the child’s best interests must be a primary consideration. The Commission takes note of the findings of Dutch Safety Board. The Commission has not been informed by the Netherlands of any activation of their contingency plan for the use of alternative reception facilities due to a temporary saturation of regular capacity under Article 32 of Directive 2024/1346. It continues to monitor implementation of the EU asylum acquis by all Member States, including reception conditions, and remains in contact with relevant national authorities. The Commission takes note of the European Union Agency for Asylum’s 2025 pilot monitoring findings in the Netherlands, including the observations about the reception conditions for vulnerable applicants. The Commission is in continues dialogue and monitors the implementation of the Pact on Migration and Asylum3 by the Member States, including on its reception situation and reliance on temporary or emergency accommodation, and stands ready to provide technical, operational and financial support to address remaining gaps.
1 Directive 2013/33/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 June 2013 laying down standards

for the reception of applicants for international protection (recast), OJ L 180, 29.6.2013. 2 Directive (EU) 2024/1346 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 laying down standards for the reception of applicants for international protection, OJ L, 2024/1346, 22.5.2024. 3 https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies/migration-and-asylum/pact-migration-and-asylum_en.
